Generated from spytial-core 6.0.0's language manifest, so every key, vocabulary, bound, default, and selector arity below is the engine's own description of the language (dated 2026-08-25). Keys are the Rust spellings; `negated = true` is spytial-core's `hold: never`. Where a selector lists more than one accepted shape, the first is the one the field is designed for. spytial-core's own guides: [YAML reference](https://github.com/sidprasad/spytial-core/blob/main/docs/YAML_SPECIFICATION.md), [constraints](https://sidprasad.github.io/spytial-core/#/constraints), [directives](https://sidprasad.github.io/spytial-core/#/directives), [selectors](https://sidprasad.github.io/spytial-core/#/selectors).

## Constraints

### `#[orientation(…)]`

Place the two ends of each selected tuple relative to one another. _(a layout constraint; takes `negated = true`)_

```text
#[orientation(selector = "parent", directions = ["above"])]
```

- `selector`: selector; required. Returns (source, target) pairs. The constraint applies to each pair. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
  - binary (2 columns): Each tuple is one (first, last) pair, and the constraint applies to it.
  - n-ary (3 or more columns): Accepted: the pair is the tuple's first and last atom. The columns between are ignored.
- `directions`: one or more of `above`, `below`, `left`, `right`, `directlyAbove`, `directlyBelow`, `directlyLeft`, `directlyRight`; required. Where the TARGET sits relative to the SOURCE. `directions: [above]` on selector `parent` places each tuple's target above its source. The `directly*` variants additionally enforce axis alignment. The direction is target-relative-to-source. Getting this backwards is the most common spec bug — transpose the selector (`~parent`) rather than flipping the direction if the relation reads the other way. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
- `negated`: `true` asserts the relationship must *not* hold (spytial-core's `hold: never`).

> Contradictory direction sets are rejected at parse time: `above` with `below`, `left` with `right`, and a `directly*` variant combined with anything other than its own non-direct counterpart. Values outside the listed set are NOT rejected — they parse and then match nothing.

### `#[align(…)]`

Put the selected atoms on a shared horizontal or vertical line. _(a layout constraint; takes `negated = true`)_

```text
#[align(selector = "siblings", direction = "horizontal")]
```

- `selector`: selector; required. Returns the pairs of atoms to align with one another. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
  - binary (2 columns): Each tuple is one (first, last) pair, and the constraint applies to it.
  - n-ary (3 or more columns): Accepted: the pair is the tuple's first and last atom. The columns between are ignored.
- `direction`: one of `horizontal`, `vertical`; required. `horizontal` gives the atoms a shared Y coordinate; `vertical` a shared X coordinate. An unrecognized value is a parse error. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
- `negated`: `true` asserts the relationship must *not* hold (spytial-core's `hold: never`).

### `#[cyclic(…)]`

Arrange the selected atoms around the perimeter of a circle, in the order the selector defines. _(a layout constraint; takes `negated = true`)_

```text
#[cyclic(selector = "nextState", direction = "clockwise")]
```

- `selector`: selector; required. Returns (a, b) pairs meaning "b follows a around the circle". _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
  - binary (2 columns): Each tuple is one (first, last) pair, and the constraint applies to it.
  - n-ary (3 or more columns): Accepted: the pair is the tuple's first and last atom. The columns between are ignored.
- `direction`: one of `clockwise`, `counterclockwise`; default `clockwise`. Which way the cycle runs.
- `negated`: `true` asserts the relationship must *not* hold (spytial-core's `hold: never`).

> Two cyclic constraints on the same selector with different directions is a parse error. An unrecognized direction string is not rejected at parse time.

### `#[group(…)]`

Draw a hull around a set of atoms. For tuples (a, b), (a, c), … the group is keyed by `a` and contains {b, c, …}. _(a layout constraint; takes `negated = true`)_

```text
#[group(selector = "Team.members", name = "Team")]
```

- `selector`: selector; required. First column is the group key, second the members. A unary selector builds a single unkeyed group. A `group` with neither `selector` nor `field` is silently dropped — it matches neither grouping form. That is the one case where omitting this field is not an error but a no-op.
  - binary (2 columns): One group per distinct first atom: the first column is the key, the last the members. The group is named `<name>[<key>]`, which is what a keyed `inferredEdge` `draw` end attaches to.
  - n-ary (3 or more columns): As binary — the key is the tuple's first atom and the member its last, ignoring the columns between.
  - unary (1 column): One single group holding every selected atom, with no key. It is named `<name>` with no `[key]` suffix, and a `draw` end naming it attaches there whatever the end's atom is.
- `name`: string; required. Display name on the group, and the handle an `inferredEdge` `draw` endpoint refers to. Required unless the constraint is negated (`hold: never`), where a name is generated. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
- `add_edge`: one of `none`, `togroup`, `fromgroup`; or the `add_edge(…)` block, which also styles it (see Style blocks); default `none`. Draw a connector between the group key and the group: `togroup` points key → group, `fromgroup` points group → key, `none` draws nothing. The legacy boolean `true` is still accepted and means `togroup`. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_
- `text_style`: `text_style(…)` block. The group's own label. Only `color` applies today — group labels auto-fit their box, so `size` is reserved.
- `negated`: `true` asserts the relationship must *not* hold (spytial-core's `hold: never`).

### `#[size(…)]`

Set the width and height of matching nodes, in pixels. _(a layout constraint)_

```text
#[size(selector = "ImportantNode", width = 150, height = 80)]
```

- `width`: number greater than 0; required. Node width in pixels. Required, and must be a number greater than 0. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
- `height`: number greater than 0; required. Node height in pixels. Required, and must be a number greater than 0. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
- `selector`: selector. Which nodes to resize. Omit to resize every node.
  - unary (1 column): The nodes to resize.

> `hold: never` is not supported and is silently ignored.

### `#[hide_atom(…)]`

Remove matching atoms from the diagram. _(a layout constraint)_

```text
#[hide_atom(selector = "HelperNode")]
```

- `selector`: selector; required. Which atoms to hide.
  - unary (1 column): The atoms to hide.

> `hold: never` is not supported and is silently ignored. Hiding an atom that a layout constraint places, or that a group contains, makes the spec unsatisfiable: the layout reports a hidden-node conflict and draws a counterfactual with the conflicting atoms outlined. Hiding a keyed group's key is fine — the key is not inside the group.

## Directives

### `#[attribute(…)]`

Render a relation as a key-value line on its source node instead of as an edge.

```text
#[attribute(field = "age", selector = "Person")]
```

- `field`: relation (field) name; required. The relation to fold into the source node. Its edges are removed from the graph.
- `selector`: selector. Apply only to these source atoms. Omit to apply to every source atom.
  - unary (1 column): The set of source atoms the directive is narrowed to.
- `filter`: selector. Apply only to the (source, target, …) tuples this selector returns. Use it to scope a directive to part of a relation, e.g. only the tuples whose value is True.
  - n-ary (2 or more columns): A tuple matches on its first and last atom, so a longer tuple filters the same relation ends a pair would. A unary result matches nothing — the directive is then scoped to no tuples at all.
- `text_style`: `text_style(…)` block. This attribute line's own styling.

> Multiple targets for the same source become a list. Unlike `tag`, this removes the edge.

### `#[flag(…)]`

Toggle a whole-diagram rendering behaviour.

```text
#[flag(name = "hideDisconnectedBuiltIns")]
```

- `name`: one of `hideDisconnected`, `hideDisconnectedBuiltIns`; required. `hideDisconnected` hides every atom with no edges; `hideDisconnectedBuiltIns` hides only the disconnected built-in atoms (Int, String, …). Any other value is silently ignored.

> Written as a bare scalar: `- flag: hideDisconnected`, not a mapping.

### `#[atom_color(…)]`

Set the color of matching atoms. _(**deprecated**, rewrites to `#[atom_style]`)_

```text
#[atom_color(selector = "Person", value = "#ff5733")]
```

- `value`: color; required. Any CSS color. Applies to the node's outline, not its fill.
- `selector`: selector; required. Which atoms to recolor. Omitting it drops the directive — it never means "every atom".
  - unary (1 column): The atoms to recolor.

### `#[atom_style(…)]`

Style matching atoms. An atom is a composite of an interior fill, an outline, an icon, and its label, so each is its own block.

```text
#[atom_style(selector = "Person", border_style(color = "#0369a1"))]
```

- `selector`: selector. Which atoms to style. Omit to style every atom.
  - unary (1 column): The atoms this rule styles.
- `fill_style`: `fill_style(…)` block. The node's interior fill.
- `border_style`: `border_style(…)` block. The node's outline.
- `icon_style`: `icon_style(…)` block. An icon drawn on the node.
- `text_style`: `text_style(…)` block. The node's own label.
- `show_label`: `true` or `false`; default `true`. Whether the atom's label is drawn. Independent of the icon: `iconStyle.placement` controls the icon's geometry, this controls the label.

> Rules compose: a supertype selector already returns subtype atoms, so a `Node` rule and a `RedNode` rule both apply to a RedNode atom and their set properties gap-fill each other. Two rules setting the SAME property to DIFFERENT values is a hard error at layout time — styles never silently override.

### `#[icon(…)]`

Assign an icon to matching atoms. _(**deprecated**, rewrites to `#[atom_style]`)_

```text
#[icon(selector = "Person", path = "person", show_labels = true)]
```

- `selector`: selector; required. Which atoms get the icon. Omitting it drops the directive entirely — it never means "every atom".
  - unary (1 column): The atoms that get the icon.
- `path`: icon name, icon-pack reference, URL, or path; required. Bundled name, icon-pack reference, URL, or path. Omitting it drops the directive.
- `show_labels`: `true` or `false`; default `false`. Whether the atom's label is drawn alongside the icon.

### `#[edge_style(…)]`

Style the edges of a relation: the drawn line, the label, and visibility.

```text
#[edge_style(field = "parent", line_style(color = "blue", pattern = "dashed"))]
```

- `field`: relation (field) name; required. The relation whose edges this styles.
- `selector`: selector. Apply only to edges whose source atom is in this set. Omit to apply to every source atom.
  - unary (1 column): The set of source atoms the directive is narrowed to.
- `filter`: selector. Apply only to the (source, target, …) tuples this selector returns. Use it to scope a directive to part of a relation, e.g. only the tuples whose value is True.
  - n-ary (2 or more columns): A tuple matches on its first and last atom, so a longer tuple filters the same relation ends a pair would. A unary result matches nothing — the directive is then scoped to no tuples at all.
- `line_style`: `line_style(…)` block. The drawn line.
- `text_style`: `text_style(…)` block. The edge label.
- `show_label`: `true` or `false`; default `true`. Whether the edge label is drawn.
- `hidden`: `true` or `false`; default `false`. Hide the edge entirely while keeping the relation in the data.
- `value`: color; the deprecated `edgeColor` form, which rewrites onto the blocks above; mixing the two shapes is a compile error. Line color.
- `style`: one of `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`; the deprecated `edgeColor` form, which rewrites onto the blocks above; mixing the two shapes is a compile error. Dash pattern. Trimmed and lowercased before matching, unlike `lineStyle.pattern`. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_
- `weight`: number greater than 0; the deprecated `edgeColor` form, which rewrites onto the blocks above; mixing the two shapes is a compile error. Line thickness in pixels. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_

> Like atomStyle, overlapping rules compose and a genuine disagreement is an error rather than a silent override.

### `#[hide_field(…)]`

Hide a relation's edges.

```text
#[hide_field(field = "internal")]
```

- `field`: relation (field) name; required. The relation to hide.
- `selector`: selector. Apply only to edges whose source atom is in this set. Omit to apply to every source atom.
  - unary (1 column): The set of source atoms the directive is narrowed to.
- `filter`: selector. Hide only the tuples this selector returns.
  - n-ary (2 or more columns): A tuple matches on its first and last atom, so a longer tuple filters the same relation ends a pair would. A unary result matches nothing — the directive is then scoped to no tuples at all.

### `#[inferred_edge(…)]`

Draw an edge that is not in the data, computed from a selector.

```text
#[inferred_edge(name = "reachable", selector = "^parent", line_style(color = "gray", pattern = "dotted"))]
```

- `name`: string; required. The label drawn on the edge.
- `selector`: selector; required. Returns the (source, target) pairs to connect. May be unary when `draw` is given — the single atom then feeds both ends.
  - binary (2 columns): One edge per tuple, from its first atom to its last.
  - n-ary (3 or more columns): One edge from the tuple's first atom to its last. Unlike the constraints, the columns between are not discarded: their labels are appended to the edge label as `<name>[m1,m2]`.
  - unary (1 column); needs `draw`: One edge per atom, the atom feeding both ends — the shape `draw: _ -> <group>` needs, connecting each atom to its own group. Without `draw` a unary selector draws nothing at all: the engine reads this field as tuples, and single-atom tuples are dropped before any edge is made.
- `draw`: string. Reinterpret what each end attaches to, as `<end> -> <end>`. Each end is `_` (the atom itself, the default) or the name of a `group` constraint, in which case the end attaches to that group's hull. The left end applies to the first atom of each tuple, the right end to the last. Parsed strictly: a value that is not a string, or that does not contain exactly one `->`, is a parse error. A group name that no `group` constraint defines is not — it raises a warning (code `unresolved-reference`, specType `inferredEdge`) and the edge is skipped at layout time, so a fragment that names a group defined in another fragment still parses. `draw` never reorders — transpose the selector (`~connected`) to flip an edge. _(a bad value makes spytial-core reject the whole spec)_
- `line_style`: `line_style(…)` block. The drawn line.
- `text_style`: `text_style(…)` block. The edge label.

> Using any of the legacy inline `color`/`style`/`weight`/`highlight` keys raises a deprecation warning with specType `inferredEdge`. The block form wins when both are given. If an end's atom keys no group of that name in a given instance, that one edge is skipped with a console warning — data-dependent, not a spec error.

### `#[tag(…)]`

Add a computed key-value line to matching nodes, without touching the graph structure.

```text
#[tag(to_tag = "Person", name = "age", value = "age")]
```

- `to_tag`: selector; required. Which atoms receive the tag.
  - unary (1 column): The atoms that receive the tag.
- `name`: string; required. The label shown before the value.
- `value`: selector; required. Evaluated per tagged atom; its result becomes the value. A binary result shows as `name: value`; a longer tuple shows one line per tuple, as `name[k1][k2]: value`. A unary result tags each selected atom with its own label.
  - n-ary (2 or more columns): One line per tuple whose first atom is the tagged atom: the last column is the value and any columns between become the key, as `name[k1][k2]: value`. A binary result is the plain `name: value` case.
  - unary (1 column): A membership tag: an atom in the result is tagged with its own label, as `name: <label>`. The value carries no more than "this atom is in the set".
- `text_style`: `text_style(…)` block. This tag line's own styling.

> Unlike `attribute`, tags do not remove edges.

## Style blocks

Blocks are written as nested groups that mirror the YAML: `line_style(color = "gray", pattern = "dotted")`. Every leaf is optional.

### `line_style(…)`

Styling for an edge's drawn line. Reused by edgeStyle, inferredEdge, and a group's addEdge connector.

- `color`: color. Any CSS color.
- `pattern`: one of `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`. Dash pattern of the line. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_
- `weight`: number greater than 0. Line thickness in pixels. Must be > 0; a non-positive or non-numeric weight is dropped. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_
- `highlight`: color. A wider, translucent underlay drawn beneath the line. Orthogonal to color and pattern.

### `text_style(…)`

Styling for a label. Reused by every form that renders text — an atom's own label, attribute and tag lines, edge labels, and a group label.

- `size`: one of `small`, `normal`, `large`; default `normal`. Font-size tier relative to the node label: `large` renders bigger than the label, `normal` smaller, `small` smaller still. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_
- `color`: color. Any CSS color. Unset inherits the node label color, so dark mode still adapts.

### `border_style(…)`

An atom's outline.

- `color`: color. Any CSS color.
- `width`: number greater than 0. Outline thickness in pixels. Must be > 0; anything else is dropped. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_

### `fill_style(…)`

An atom's interior fill. Opt-in: the default look is unfilled, with only the border and label marking the node.

- `color`: color. Any CSS color.

### `icon_style(…)`

An icon drawn on an atom. Every leaf is optional, including `path`, so a supertype rule can supply the icon and a subtype rule tune only its opacity.

- `path`: icon name, icon-pack reference, URL, or path. A bundled icon name (`person`), an icon-pack reference (`bi:person-fill`), a URL, or a path. Resolved to a concrete URL or data URI at parse time. An iconStyle with no path draws nothing.
- `placement`: one of `full`, `badge`; default `full`. `full` — the icon occupies the box, which stays transparent unless a fillStyle.color is given. `badge` — a small marker in the top-right corner, secondary to the label. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_
- `opacity`: number between 0 and 1; default `1`. Alpha in [0,1]. Out-of-range values are dropped rather than clamped. Fade a `full` icon to use it as a watermark behind the label. _(spytial-core drops a bad value silently)_

### `add_edge(…)` (on `#[group]`)

Block form also styles the connector, which is an edge and so takes the shared edge blocks: `{ points: <direction>, lineStyle: {…}, textStyle: {…} }`.

- `points`: one of `none`, `togroup`, `fromgroup`; default `none`. The connector direction — the same value the bare string form carries.
- `line_style`: `line_style(…)` block. The connector's line.
- `text_style`: `text_style(…)` block. The connector's label.

## Deprecated forms

Each still compiles and still works, with a compile-time deprecation warning naming the replacement; `#[allow(deprecated)]` on the type keeps one deliberately.

- `#[icon(…)]` → `#[atom_style]`. The single `showLabels` boolean drove label visibility and icon geometry at once. atomStyle splits those into two independent knobs, which is what makes a faded watermark, or a hidden label with no icon, expressible. Mapping: `path` → `icon_style.path`; `show_labels: false` → `show_label: false + icon_style.placement: full`; `show_labels: true` → `show_label: true + icon_style.placement: badge`.
- `#[atom_color(…)]` → `#[atom_style]`. atomStyle expresses the same recolor and also reaches the fill, the icon, and the label. The rewrite is border-preserving, so an existing diagram is unchanged. Mapping: `value` → `border_style.color`.
- `#[edge_style]` written with `value`/`style`/`weight` → `#[edge_style]`. edgeStyle groups the same knobs into the shared lineStyle/textStyle blocks that every other form uses. Mapping: `value` → `line_style.color`; `style` → `line_style.pattern`; `weight` → `line_style.weight`; `highlight` → `line_style.highlight`.
